headline: Approved Steven Neal as Deputy Commissioner of Water Supply, and awarded $24,870 water tank cleaning contract.
summary: Updates covered water main projects on Main St., Water St., and Exeter St., plus a July 31 Mass DEP notice of non-compliance at the East Wastewater Treatment Plant. Staff said lower sewage flows have made the plant harder to run, and Arcadis is designing blower upgrades. Two treatment operators resigned, and the distribution system manager job is open.
decisions: Approved the July 15, 2026 meeting minutes unanimously.
Approved Steven Neal as Deputy Commissioner of Water Supply, 5-0.
Awarded the water storage tank cleaning bid to the lower bidder at $24,870.

decision_titles: Appointment of Steven Neal as Deputy Commissioner of Water Supply
plain_text:
Water/Wastewater Commission
Meeting Minutes
September 16th, 2026
                          Legislative Building, City Hall Campus
700 Main St, Fitchburg MA 01420
______________________________________________________________________________
A meeting for the City of Fitchburg Water/Wastewater Commission was held on Wednesday September 
16, 2026 at the Legislative Building, City Hall Campus, 700 Main St. Fitchburg, MA 01420
The meeting commenced at 5:03 PM
Members present:   Rick Healey, Chairman
                                    Nicholas Erickson, Commissioner of Public Works
                                    George Seiner, Commission Member
                                    Michael Mclaughlin, Commission Member
       Gary Withington, Commission Member                                    
                                    Joseph Byrne, Commission Member
Others present:       John M. Deline Jr, Deputy Commissioner Wastewater Division
      Steve Neal, Distribution System Manager 
                                   Brian Nolan, Superintendent East Wastewater Treatment Plant 
Absent:                      Jason Lefferts, Commission Member
Item #1
Approval of meeting minutes:  Motion to approve the July 15, 2026 meeting minutes was made and 
seconded, minutes were approved unanimously.
Item #2
Public Forum:  None
Item #3
Water Division:
 Deputy Commissioner of Water Supply –
 DPW Commissioner Nick Erickson – Steve Neal is here to give an update on behalf of 
the water division, but before we get into that the first item on the water divisions list 
of topics is the Deputy Commissioner of Water Supply. As you all know, last meeting, 
we had a candidate in front of you. A request was made to do a little more vetting of 
that candidate. Based on the things that were said during that meeting we followed 
through with that request. We felt that he was not a good fit for the city and ultimately
decided to rescind our offer of employment to that candidate. Tonight, in front of you, 
we have Steve Neal. The city has made an offer to Steve contingent upon successful 
appointment by the water/wastewater commission. I’ve handed out a copy of his 
resume for your review. If you would like to ask Steve any questions tonight during this
meeting, he’s offered to answer any you may have. 
 Steve – Hi, as Nick said my name is Steve Neal. I was born and raised in Fitchburg, went
to Fitchburg schools, graduated from Monty Tech and lived here until about the time I 
got married and bought a house in Winchendon. I started in the water field in 
September of 1994 in the town of Ashburnham. Worked my way up the ladder then 
moved to the city of Gardner with united water which is a private contractor who is 
now Viola. Worked in the treatment plants there as an operator and then Winchendon 
hired United water under an emergency contract. I moved there as distribution and 
sewer collections chief operator until the five-year contract end in 2013. John was 
DPW director for the town of Winchendon and him and I worked together for me to 
stay with the town and leave Gardner and then I was there until 2017. John had left 
Winchendon and had come to Fitchburg. We talked back and forth about myself 
coming to Fitchburg as Distribution System Manager, which I did and have been here 
since.
 Chairman Rick Healey – Thank you. Do you have questions? Does anybody have any 
questions for Steve? Steve, I see you’ve got a lot of experience in a lot of different 
towns. Tell me about your comfort level is as far as you’re going to be speaking before 
the city council and that sort of thing. What experience have you had like that?
 Steve – I’ve had experience mostly in Ashburnham, working with selectmen and the 
town manager, town meetings and the water/sewer board meetings.
 Rick – Does anybody else have any questions?
 Gary – So the 10 years before I retired, I worked with Steve. I think he would be a very 
good fit for this position.
 Rick – Thank you, we appreciate hearing that. Any other thoughts?
 Nick – I just wanted to add that as distribution system manager, I’ve worked with Steve
since he started here in the city of Fitchburg and he’s always been very good to work 
with. He’s very diligent about making sure that any task assigned to him gets done. 
He’s a very good communicator as far as keeping people in the loop when there’s a 
water main break or some other issue with the water distribution system. It’s also 
important to note that when John was absent, either vacation or sick, Steve would 
usually be tasked with filling in on a temporary basis. So, he’s had experience running 
the water division in the absence of the deputy commissioner and we know he can 
definitely do the job. So, I think he will be a good fit.
 Rick – I think it’s quite clear that he appears to have the support of the balance of the 
staff, from what I understand. I think what we are looking for at this point is not a
recommendation to the city council, this is a recommendation to take Steve on as the 
Deputy Commissioner of water supply?
 Nick – Correct. So, this position specifically is not appointed by the city council. It’s only
subject to confirmation by this group. So tonight, we would be seeking a motion and 
approval for that confirmation and that would complete the last step in Steve’s offer of
employment. His offer is contingent upon this body’s approval.
 Rick – Are there any other questions?
 Mike – I don’t really have a question, if we’re coming on Nick’s recommendation and 
other board members, it looks like Steve has a lot of great qualifications and he’s 
somewhat local. I think that will help with response time because I know John, you had
mentioned that on the water side that’s a little more crucial.
 John - Yeah, I think it’s important for somebody to reside fairly close within a half hour 
or so.
 Rick – I’d like to entertain a motion to approve the appointment of Steven Neal. Would
someone like to make that motion?
 Gary – I’ll make that motion to approve Steven Neal.
 Rick – Do I have a second?
 Mike – I’ll second that motion.
 Rick – Any discussion? Hearing none. All those in favor?
 Nick – yes
 Mike – yes
 Gary – yes
 George – yes
 Rick – yes, Thank you. Motion carries 5-0. Welcome Steve!
 Staffing update – Steve let the commission know that we recently had two treatment 
operators turn in their resignation. One moved out of state and the other took a position 
with a treatment plant closer to his home. We are currently advertising for these positions 
and have had a couple of applicants apply and plan on doing interviews soon to get those 
positions filled. My old position of distribution system manager is now open, and has been 
posted and we have received one applicant.
 Water Main Replacement Projects
1. Main St. Water Main - J.A. Polito is finishing up this project. Main lines are done 
except one last minute one at 356 Main St., which they will be finishing up tomorrow. 
The still have a few sidewalk spots that need restoration, and then will be moving on 
to paving.
2. Water St. Water Main – MIG corporation who is the contractor for this project started 
laying both new water mains. A new 12” on the low system and a new 16” on the high 
system. They currently have about 200 ft installed on each one and the total length is 
about 510 ft. So, they are making some progress. I haven’t heard of any issues with 
traffic, or the plaza on temp water mains.
Mike – I just have one comment. We have a lot going on in the city, but several days ago we 
had a rain event and there are some major projects and one of them is on Water St. and 
there the washout was incredible. We had trenches that were very deep in front of the 
market basket entrance, and also where Montouri’s used to be. In front of that gas station 
there was a trench that never got patched. I think if we could be a little more conscious 
about letting those guys now that if they don’t patch those and leave them open it gets
pretty bad on the weekends. I had the experience of going through the one on Water St. 
and it was pretty dangerous for a lot of cars.
Nick – So they are typically instructed to pave every Friday and not leave open tranches 
going into the weekend, especially if there is a rain event. So, I will address that. We have 
weekly meetings with MASS Dot and the contractor MIG.
3. Exeter St. Water Main – Contractor GVC is in the process of replacing about 1,920 ft of
old 6” tuberculated water main. I believe today, I didn’t have a chance to check with 
them this afternoon, I believe they made the final connection and will be moving on to 
pressure testing, chlorination and bacteria that section. Then they will connect people 
to the new main and get them off of the temporary water main.
4. High St. (Elm St. to Mechanic St.) – Polito replaced about 460 ft of old 8” cast iron with
a new 12” from the intersection at Elm St. up to Mechanic St. They made the final 
connection this morning, the main’s filled in and this afternoon they were pressure 
testing. As long as that passed, they will be moving on to chlorinating and then 
bacteria testing, and then get that up and running so we can get out of the way for 
GVC coming up Mechanic St. with the CSO project and paving of that area.
5. Boulder Dr. Water Main (Cushing St. to Water St. Bridge) – J. A. Polito will be putting 
in a PRV (pressure reducing valve) where the low water system meets the high-water 
system just up from Kimball St. between Kimball and Payson St., they will be replacing 
a section of a couple hundred feet of old 6” main with new 8” from Payson down. 
Installing a pressure reducing valve connected to the low system which services the 
lower end of Laurel St., South St., Cross St. and Walnut St. to add a feed for emergency 
purposes because currently the only feed is from Water St. across Walnut St. They 
have temps set up for the 3 or 4 homes that will be affected. That’s all been tested and
by the end of this week beginning of next week they will tie those homes to the 
temporary lines and install a couple hundred feet along with the pressure reducing 
valve. 
 Montachusett Industrial Park Pump Station – This is the fire pump replacement project that
John started. All the bid specs were done, they were posted on everything with the State 
today, and we’ll wait to see what we get. Bid openings are scheduled for October 14th at 
2PM.
 Water Storage Tanks – We had two bids for this, they were priced pretty far apart. The 
lower bidder was $24,870 and the second bid was $97,350. We spent a lot of time 
conversing with the low bidder to make sure that they completely understand what the bid 
is and we were happy with it and what we talked about so we awarded the bid to them. 
They plan on starting the tank cleaning September 28th.
Item #4
Wastewater Division:
 East Wastewater Treatment Plant – Mass DEP NON – John let the commission know that they 
received a notice of non-compliance from Mass DEP a few weeks back about some exceedances 
at the east wastewater treatment plant.  He asked Brian the chief operator to speak on this 
item.
 Brian – Hi I’m Brian Nolan, I’m the superintendent at the east Fitchburg wastewater 
treatment facility. On July 31st we received a letter of non-compliance from Mass DEP. 
Something that’s happened to the treatment plant with great success of the sewer 
separation project is we are no longer seeing the flows that we once saw coming into
the treatment plant on a regular basis. Its significantly reduced, we currently have one 
quarter of the treatment facility online. It’s completely unprecedented. We have never 
seen this before, and so we’ve been trying to adapt to this new way of operating. We 
felt like we were kind of losing our grip around the treatment process in 2025. So, in 
September of 2025 we contracted with Arcadis Engineering to do a treatment 
optimization study to figure out where we should be. One of the things that was 
wonderful about us contracting with them, is that when we did get this notice of non-
compliance we were ahead of the game. Arcadis wound up drafting all of the 
responses to Mass DEP. Some of the things that they touched upon include a detailed 
response to planned actions to correct the identified violations, a schedule to correct 
the violations and a plan for additional work. We do need to upgrade some of our 
blowers. Running the treatment plant takes a tremendous amount of dissolved oxygen 
and we use the blowers to blow this air into these huge tanks. One of our blower 
systems is just severely outdated. We need to have fine tuning of the air in order to 
achieve proper biological nutrient removal. That’s what Arcadis is working on right 
now, trying to get the design plan as quickly as possible. Arcadis feels confident that 
they can include this in our current SCADA upgrade, which will go out to bid in January.
 Mike – Just a simple question.  How are we not in compliance?
 Brian – We have to test daily for all sorts of different things, and one of them is TSS 
(total suspended solids), and so with the design flow being so much greater than the 
flow we are receiving. Part of the system we are currently using, has a capacity of 
about 2.6 million gallons, and we’re receiving in between 3 and 4 million gallons per 
day. These tanks are supposed to refresh much faster than that, so when you put 
sludge in the tank and just let it sit there for six hours, it kind of releases and floats up 
even if you had settled if down. It deteriorates the quality of our effluent and we 
measure that in TSS. So that’s one of the violations we get whacked with. Our summer 
permit is 10 milligrams per liter. It’s very low, and very hard to reach that when we 
don’t have flow moving though the plant constantly refreshing the sludge in the water.
 Mike – So we are having great success with all this work you guys are doing and the 
DEP has mandated, and now we are being penalized, it’s crazy.
 Rick – Are we being penalized?
 Brian – No, no, we’re currently not in any danger of that. We’ve always reported 
honestly, we haven’t hidden anything from Mass DEP. When we started to work with 
Arcadis, I let the DEP know that we were having trouble and were going to be working 
with them to fix the problem.
 Mike – I guess I used the wrong word, penalized, but we are getting our hand slapped, 
and it sounds like this has been a tremendous success. Right?
 Brian – Absolutely. So, we used to see around 9 MGD at this time of year, and we are 
like around 4 MGD. You know that’s significant.
 Mike – And were not even done yet, right?
 Nick – Right, we still have another 4 years’ worth of separation projects, including the 
largest project which is coming up. So that will remove probably the largest amount of 
flow from the system as far as infiltration and inflow go.
 Rick – Any other questions?
 Brian – I welcome everyone to come take a tour anytime.
 Rick – Thanks!
John continued adding, wastewater had gotten ahead of it last year by hiring Arcadis for the 
optimization study so, we’re fortunate we can include the lower upgrades with the SCADA 
project vs. a whole separate project. So that will expedite it because we’re already 
underway with SCADA, the designs like 60 to 70% complete. So, adding this to help with 
that, we should be able to address these items. Long term, of course we need to make these
changes to the plant, but it’s going to save us money. We just need to adapt to small flows 
coming in. We have to address those types of operational issues with the plant so we can 
remain in compliance.
 Westminster IMA (inter-municipal agreement) – We are working on this with the mayor’s 
office. So that’s going to be going on the next few weeks. This expired a little while ago and 
Westminster seems to be looking to increase their allotted flows. This would help us 
generate more revenue and you know we have the capacity at the plant of course. So, we’ll 
work with them on that.
 CSO Project updates –
1. CSO 032, GVC is supposed to be completed this project by the end of this year. 
That’s where they’ve been working around the upper common, they still have some 
more work to do on Wood Pl. and Main St., but we are hoping by the end of this 
construction season they will have completed that. We are going to be paving some 
of the sections up in the High St., Marshall St. area that were done last year. 
Everything’s settled and starting next week, we’ll be paving areas up there, milling 
and paving and some reclamation on the streets. Next year once other sections 
have settled with GVC up on Mechanic St., we’ll do the final paving next year.
Mike – What is the scheduled for Main St. to be paved?
John – I know the water projects will be doing some of the paving, we still have work to do on 
Main St. from Wood Pl. up a little way and down a little way as part of the GVC project, and the 
contractor Polito also has some work to do on Main St. so, that section won’t be final paved.
Nick – We just met with Weston & Sampson today to finalize what we want to see for trench 
restoration. They are going to do a mill and pave from Newton Pl. moving east, encompassing 
their trench in the westbound lane from the center line to the curb. We might do some 
additional paving depending on whether or not we receive a grant through Mass works for the 
Moran Square project. If we do not receive that grant, we will do some extra paving in the 
Moran Square area because its very rough over there and we’ll have a milling machine and 
paver out there anyways. The area west of Newton Pl. is going to be part of GVC’s work that’s 
still outstanding that they are planning to do this year. We won’t be milling and paving anything 
until GVC is done and out of there. We will likely shift that paving responsibility onto GVC since 
they are doing all the work around the upper common and basically right out in front of city hall.
So, that will be a little further down the road. Polito will be milling and paving those trenches 
that they’ve cut from Newton Pl. moving east to Lunenburg St. and Summer St.
2. CSO 045/083, J.A. Polito has this contract. Part of the work comes up through 
Newton Pl. over to 166 Boulder Dr. with a 60” pipe that’s got to go up through 
there. So, they will be starting that, and then in the coming weeks, they have a 
couple years to finish that, so its going to take a while.
3. CSO 004, this project is like easterly of the Depot St. area up around Franklin Rd. 
Weston & Sampson completed the investigation up there this spring and is now 
working on the design for all of it. This will be the next project that goes out to bid.
 Staffing update –We had one senior operator who left and went to upper Blackstone for a 
higher rate of pay. We have had some people move around within the division. Our chemist 
will become a senior operator and one of our wastewater operators will become a senior 
operator. We hope to fill those slots so we can make sure all shifts are filled. We have one 
new hire who will be a wastewater operator and starts on Monday. We are still looking at 
reducing operations by one shift and are working out things with the union through 
negotiations that we have going on. That will help with the number of personnel that we 
need as well as overtime. Eventually with the SCADA upgrades we will look at more 
automation with the plant. We have 3 or 4 people that are pretty much set to retire come 
January or next spring, so, we’ll have to work on filling those positions as well as time goes 
by.
Other Business:
 The Water/Wastewater Commission will next meet at 5:00 pm on Wednesday October 21, 2026
at the Legislative Building, City Hall Campus 700 Main St. Fitchburg, MA.
Meeting adjourned at 5:34 PM
